headline: 8th title: India win Women's Asia Cup after crushing Sri Lanka
summary: A record-breaking opening stand and a dominant spin attack led India to a 72-run victory in the final.
details: India secured their eighth Women's Asia Cup title and fourth in the T20 format by defeating Sri Lanka by 72 runs at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium on Sunday.
Shafali Verma (68 off 39) and Smriti Mandhana (59 off 39) set the stage with a record opening partnership of 129 runs, the highest in Women's T20 Asia Cup history.
The explosive start helped India post a formidable total of 183-5 in their allotted overs.
Sri Lanka struggled to build momentum in the chase, eventually being bundled out for 111 runs despite India dropping five catches.
India's spin attack proved decisive, with Shree Charani taking 4-20 and Deepti Sharma claiming 3-19.
With this victory, India now leads Sri Lanka 6-1 in Asia Cup final meetings.
caption:
A record-breaking start and a dominant spin attack! India claims their 8th Women's Asia Cup title.

India secured their eighth Women's Asia Cup title and fourth in the T20 format by defeating Sri Lanka by 72 runs at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium on Sunday.

Shafali Verma (68 off 39) and Smriti Mandhana (59 off 39) set the stage with a record opening partnership of 129 runs, the highest in Women's T20 Asia Cup history.

The explosive start helped India post a formidable total of 183-5 in their allotted overs.

Sri Lanka struggled to build momentum in the chase, eventually being bundled out for 111 runs despite India dropping five catches.

India's spin attack proved decisive, with Shree Charani taking 4-20 and Deepti Sharma claiming 3-19.

With this victory, India now leads Sri Lanka 6-1 in Asia Cup final meetings.

headline_marked: 6 hours of chaos: [[Dhaka-Mymensingh train services resume]] after derailment
headline: 6 hours of chaos: Dhaka-Mymensingh train services resume after derailment
summary: A freight train wagon derailed in Gafargaon, suspending services on the busy route for six hours on Sunday evening.
details: Train services on the Dhaka-Mymensingh route resumed around 11:15 PM Sunday after a freight train wagon derailed in Gafargaon, Mymensingh.
The incident occurred around 5:15 PM in the Golabari area between Kauraid and Mashakhali railway stations.
The freight train, which had departed from Dhaka, was passing through Golabari when one of its wagons derailed, causing an immediate suspension of services on the busy route.
The derailment left several trains stranded, including the Dhaka-bound Teesta Express, which was held at Mymensingh Railway Station.
Other affected trains, including the Commuter Express, Jamalpur Express, Mohanganj Express, Agnibina Express, and Brahmaputra Express, were stranded at various stations after leaving Dhaka.
A relief train from Dhaka reached the spot at 9:30 PM to begin rescue operations, as confirmed by Mohammad Akhtar Hossain, officer-in-charge of the Mymensingh Railway Police Station.

Train services on the Dhaka-Mymensingh route resumed around 11:15 PM Sunday after a freight train wagon derailed in Gafargaon, Mymensingh.

The incident occurred around 5:15 PM in the Golabari area between Kauraid and Mashakhali railway stations.

The freight train, which had departed from Dhaka, was passing through Golabari when one of its wagons derailed, causing an immediate suspension of services on the busy route.

The derailment left several trains stranded, including the Dhaka-bound Teesta Express, which was held at Mymensingh Railway Station.

Other affected trains, including the Commuter Express, Jamalpur Express, Mohanganj Express, Agnibina Express, and Brahmaputra Express, were stranded at various stations after leaving Dhaka.

A relief train from Dhaka reached the spot at 9:30 PM to begin rescue operations, as confirmed by Mohammad Akhtar Hossain, officer-in-charge of the Mymensingh Railway Police Station.
